zakat.claim_evidence: The National Association of Muslim Lawyers (NAML) is a 501(c)(6) organization. ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer states that 'Donations to this organization are not tax deductible'. There is no explicit mention of 'zakat' on NAML's website or donation pages in the provided search results. While NAML partners with the Islamic Scholarship Fund and Muslim Advocates (which has a statement on zakat eligibility), these are separate entities, and the evidence does not indicate that NAML itself accepts zakat. (Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Muslim_Lawyers)

rich_narrative.summary: The National Association of Muslim Lawyers operates with significant reporting gaps that limit financial transparency. No financial filings newer than FY2023 are available — donors should treat this 3-year-old financial picture with caution, as it raises severe accountability questions <cite id="2">Form 990 (2023)</cite>. The organization's core activities focus on improving the legal profession through <cite id="3">networking, mentorship, educational programs, and support for regional Muslim bar associations</cite>. Additionally, the group engages in high-level legal advocacy, having submitted amicus briefs in major litigation such as <cite id="4">IRAP v. Trump</cite> and <cite id="5">Trump v. Hawaii</cite>. However, recent financial numbers reveal instability. The organization reported <cite id="2">$85,362 in revenue for FY2023</cite>, reflecting a 7% decline from the previous year's $92,058 <cite id="2">Form 990 (2023)</cite>. Total expenses exceeded revenue in 2023 at $113,423, resulting in <cite id="2">total assets dropping to $24,723</cite>. Further, public disclosures omit the program expense breakdown entirely, making it impossible to evaluate operational spending efficiency <cite id="1">Charity Navigator</cite>.
